say: For example, Chiamaka in Onitsha supplies two laundries. Her LABSA, the sulphonic acid, is 96% strength. She needs 1.60 kg of it.

panel.heading: Chiamaka's 20 kg laundry batch
items: LABSA: 20 kg x 8% = 1.60 kg
Caustic soda: 1.60 x 0.118 = about 189 g
First addition about 90%: about 170 g
SLES 1.20 kg, soda ash 0.20 kg, CMC 60 g
Water: about 16.75 kg to reach 20 kg

say: Caustic soda turns LABSA into a strong cleaner. About 0.118 kg neutralises each kilogram of 96% LABSA, so she needs about 189 g.

say: Goggles, gloves, apron and long sleeves on. Open the window.

panel.heading: Neutralise first, then the rest
items: Full PPE on, window open
About 12 kg water, then LABSA in slowly
Caustic solution in four or five portions
Test pH: stop at about 7 to 8
Then soda ash, CMC, SLES; top up to 20 kg
Rest overnight, check pH 9 to 10, fill

panel.rule: Never rush caustic. Never lean over the drum while pouring.

say: Dish liquid touches hands for a long time, so it stops at about pH 7, with no soda ash.

panel.heading: Funke thickens with salt, step by step
items: Neutralise to about pH 7, no soda ash
Make a 25% salt solution
Add 100 g, stir, time 100 ml through a funnel
500 g: 22 seconds. 600 g: 21 seconds
Next time: stop at 500 g

say: Salt thickens it, but only up to a point. Past that point it thins again, and you cannot take the salt out. So make a 25% salt solution.

say: Your label promises 500 ml, but your scale measures weight, and dish liquid is a little heavier than water. So Funke weighs exactly 1 litre: 1,030 g. That is 1.03 g per ml.

panel.heading: Funke's bottles from a 25 kg batch
items: Density: 1,030 g per litre = 1.03 g/ml
500 ml x 1.03 = 515 g per bottle
25,000 g / 515 g = 48 full bottles
Leftover 280 g: retained sample
Tare with bottle and cap; check every tenth

say: So each 500 ml bottle gets 515 g.

panel.rule: Every customer receives what the label says.

say: Floor cleaner is a concentrate, so the dose on your label is part of the product.

For example, Rukayat in Ilorin tests her concentrate on four equal patches of a greasy restaurant kitchen floor, using a 5 litre bucket each. 1 in 100 cleans with no film. 1 in 50 is no better and leaves foam.

panel.heading: The dilution ladder test
left: 1 in 50: clean, but foam to rinse

say: So she chooses the weakest rung that still cleans well.
Her label gives the dose in millilitres, the bucket size, and a warning not to mix with bleach.
The manager can see a 4 litre keg lasts 80 kitchen buckets, which helps her sell it.

panel.heading: The dilution ladder test
left: 1 in 50: clean, but foam to rinse

say: To remember. Work from percentages to kilograms. Add caustic in portions and finish by pH. Thicken in measured steps. Fill by weight. And write clear directions with a dose and a no-mixing warning.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Batch weight x percentage = ingredient weight
Caustic in portions; finish by pH
Salt in measured steps; stop at the peak
Fill weight = label volume x density
Dose, bucket size and no-mixing on the label
